question: ap1
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out finishing within three months. Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus then washout: AP-1 binding and accessibility persistence
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) to a defined stimulus such as TPA, serum, or LPS, then wash out and run CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN and ATAC-seq at multiple time points (1 h to 14 days). Sites where AP-1 occupancy and accessibility persist after the stimulus and AP-1 protein levels have returned to baseline are candidate memory loci.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation to test maintenance versus initiation
ideas.description: Use dTAG or auxin-inducible degron knock-ins for FOS, JUN or the pioneer-like subunit, and degrade the protein either during stimulation or after memory is established. Compare ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP and RNA-seq to determine whether AP-1 is required only to establish the accessible state or also to maintain it, which is the central criterion that separates a memory mechanism from a one-time trigger.

ideas.title: Memory functional assay: primed re-stimulation response
ideas.description: Prime cells with a first stimulus, rest them for days to weeks, then re-stimulate and measure the speed and magnitude of transcription (nascent RNA, PRO-seq or 4sU-seq) compared with naive cells. Repeat with AP-1 degron or dominant-negative (A-FOS) perturbation at priming only, to test whether AP-1 is needed to encode the enhanced response.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracing across divisions
ideas.description: Perform single-cell RNA and ATAC (multiome) on primed and naive cells, with barcode lineage tracing or sister-cell pairing after division, and infer AP-1 motif activity (e.g., chromVAR). Test whether sister cells share accessibility and AP-1 activity states more than random cells do, and whether memory is heritable through mitosis and bimodal versus graded.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and locus-specific causal editing
ideas.description: Use live-cell imaging or single-molecule tracking of tagged JUN and FOS, plus CUT&RUN on mitotically arrested cells, to test whether AP-1 stays on chromatin during mitosis. Then use dCas9 or motif mutation (CRISPR editing) at selected memory enhancers to test whether the AP-1 site is necessary for the persistent accessibility and primed response, and use dCas9-KRAB to test sufficiency.
